---
name: notebook-to-streamlit
description: Use when converting analysis and functions from an existing
  Jupyter Notebook into a Streamlit app. Covers extracting notebook logic,
  mapping notebook inputs to widgets, and displaying results safely.
  Not for changing the underlying analysis or building unrelated features.
---

## Step 1 — Extract notebook logic

Read the existing Jupyter Notebook before building the app.

Identify the functions and calculations needed by the Streamlit app and reuse that logic without changing the analytical methodology.

Keep computation separate from the Streamlit interface where possible.
Functions should take inputs, perform calculations, and return results without depending on Streamlit.

Do not recreate values already provided by imported packages or change working notebook calculations unnecessarily.


## Step 2 — Map notebook inputs to Streamlit

Convert the notebook's user-adjustable inputs into appropriate Streamlit widgets.

| Notebook | Streamlit |
|---|---|
| fixed categorical input | `st.selectbox` |
| numeric input | `st.number_input` or `st.slider` |
| list/range of values | minimum and maximum widgets |
| function arguments | values collected from widgets |
| `print(result)` | `st.write`, `st.metric`, or `st.success` |
| invalid input | `st.error(...)` then `st.stop()` |

Defaults should match the notebook or imported default values where appropriate.

Validate user inputs before running the calculations.


## Step 3 — Preserve calculation behavior

The Streamlit app must use the same functions and calculation logic as the Jupyter Notebook.

When a notebook function depends on simulation or randomness, preserve the notebook's approach by using seed=1 .

Do not silently change formulas, assumptions, cost calculations, or optimization criteria when moving them into the app.


## Step 4 — Handle Streamlit reruns

Streamlit reruns the script whenever a user interacts with a widget.

If the result is generated by an `st.button(...)`, store the result in `st.session_state` so it does not disappear when another widget causes a rerun.

The button should perform the calculation and update state. Display the stored result outside the button block.



## Done when

- [ ] The original Jupyter Notebook remains unchanged and still runs
- [ ] The app uses the notebook's existing analytical logic
- [ ] Required notebook inputs are represented by appropriate widgets
- [ ] Inputs are validated before calculations run
- [ ] The main calculation runs successfully from the app
- [ ] Results remain visible after Streamlit reruns
- [ ] Simulation results are reproducible where required
- [ ] Changing user inputs changes the calculation appropriately
- [ ] The app displays the final result clearly
- [ ] No unnecessary functionality has been added
